contract: CBWeb3 Scenario B — Hub-and-spoke settlement (bridge, liquidity and reconciliation)

vectors.title: Lock spoke tCeBM and mint the Hub W-token
vectors.description: Moves value from a spoke to the Hub. Used directly by Central Banks to seed liquidity, and indirectly by the relay as step 1 of every cross-currency swap — a client never calls it as part of a payment.

preconditions.session: cookie OR bearer, carrying commercial_bank or central_bank
preconditions.reservePrelude: completed; the caller holds at least amount of spoke tCeBM

vectors.notes: The request needs ONLY amount. owner_bank_id comes from the session bankId claim and spoke_network, native_asset and mirrored_asset all come from gateway configuration — all four body fields are deprecated and sending them changes nothing. The lock and mint are ENQUEUED, not completed: poll bridge-hp-02 until bridge_state reads ACTIVE.

vectors.title: Positions come back wrapped, and carry a state vocabulary the OpenAPI omits
vectors.description: Poll after lock-mint until the position is ACTIVE, and after a cross-currency swap to confirm the bridge-out position reached BURNED or RELEASED.
vectors.notes: TWO divergences on one operation. (1) The platform document declares the 200 body as a bare JSON array; the delivered handler returns {"positions": [...]}. (2) The document's state example suggests PENDING, ACTIVE, CLOSED — PENDING and CLOSED DO NOT EXIST. The real vocabulary is LOCKING, ACTIVE, BURNING, BURNED, RELEASED, RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, and it lives only in internal/domain, so the contract publishes it in prose rather than as an enum the platform has not committed to. Never write a client state machine against the document's example.

vectors.title: Filter positions by bridge state
vectors.description: The state query parameter takes the real vocabulary from bridge-hp-02, not the document's example values.
vectors.notes: This vector deliberately authenticates with a BEARER token rather than a cookie, to exercise the RequireAnyAuth half of the surface. Filtering by PENDING or CLOSED returns an empty list rather than an error, which is exactly how a client following the document's example silently sees nothing.

vectors.title: Burn the Hub token and unlock the spoke tCeBM
vectors.description: The inverse of lock-mint for an existing position. Also enqueued rather than immediate.

preconditions.session: cookie or bearer, commercial_bank or central_bank

vectors.notes: Note the status asymmetry: lock-mint returns 201 and burn-unlock returns 200. Poll bridge-hp-02 until the state reaches BURNED or RELEASED before concluding the unwind finished.

vectors.title: Reconciliation — unexplained must be zero at rest
vectors.description: Treasury-facing. Reports the Central Bank's omnibus Hub balance, what in-flight payments legitimately still hold, and the part it cannot attribute.

preconditions.session: cookie or bearer for a Central Bank
preconditions.gateway: configured with HUB_BESU_RPC_URL, W_TOKEN_ADDRESS and this Central Bank's hub address

vectors.notes: unexplained is the number that matters and balanced is true exactly when it is zero. stranded_total is CONTEXT, not a deduction — it is already-flagged value and may be counted in unexplained too, so subtracting it double-counts. unattributed covers settled positions whose trade cost was never recorded and is deliberately excluded from expected_in_flight. This is assertion (5) of swap-hp-04.

vectors.title: Mint and approve this Central Bank's W-token for the pool
vectors.description: Corridor provisioning. Mints the caller Central Bank's own Hub W-token and approves the pool's AMM to spend it.

preconditions.session: cookie or bearer for a Central Bank

vectors.notes: 200, not 201. Supplying an optional recipient changes the semantics entirely: the tokens are minted TO that address instead of being minted and approved for the pool, and recipient is then echoed in the response. A Central Bank attempting to mint another Central Bank's token is refused 403 with CROSS_CB_MINT_PROHIBITED.

vectors.title: Commit liquidity — only pool_pair and amount are required
vectors.description: The cooperative commit-reveal path the platform's own end-to-end test uses to make a pool ACTIVE. Each Central Bank commits its own side; a Cacti watcher observes CommitMatched and the relay executes both together.

preconditions.session: cookie or bearer carrying central_bank or mlp

vectors.notes: The contract corrects an upstream over-specification here: provider_id, side and w_token_address are declared but DEPRECATED and must not be sent — the provider comes from the session, the side is an on-chain property of (pair, Central Bank) and the token address comes from gateway configuration. Only pool_pair and amount are genuinely required.

vectors.title: Poll the commit until EXECUTED
vectors.description: EXECUTED means the Cacti watcher matched both Central Banks' commits and the relay funded the pool. Only then does the pool become ACTIVE.
vectors.notes: A commit that stays PENDING means the counterpart Central Bank has not committed — check GET /api/v2/amm/pool/{pair}/status for PENDING_COUNTERPART. The list form of this endpoint (GET /api/v2/amm/liquidity/commits) returns a BARE array, unlike currencies, pairs and bridge positions, which are all wrapped. There is no consistency to rely on; check per endpoint.

vectors.title: Lock-mint without amount is 400
vectors.description: amount is the single required field and is validated at the gateway.
vectors.notes: The 400 on this route carries the bare {error} shape, not the richer {error, error_code} the swap family uses. Two error models coexist on the same /api/v2 prefix.

vectors.title: Lock-mint beyond the daily transfer limit is 422
vectors.description: The transfer limit applies to the bridge as well as to swaps.

preconditions.transferLimit: exists for this participant and is already exhausted

vectors.notes: The same 422 also covers a failure of the lock-and-enqueue step itself, so a 422 here does not uniquely identify a limit breach. Undeclared upstream; observed in the delivered handler.

vectors.title: Burn-unlock on an unknown position is 422, because there is no 404
vectors.description: The bridge family declares no 404 anywhere. An identifier that does not resolve fails the burn-and-enqueue step and surfaces as an unprocessable entity.
vectors.notes: Note this 422 returns the BARE {error} body, while the 422 on lock-mint returns {error, error_code}. Two sibling operations, two error shapes. Assert the status code.

vectors.title: Positions with no credential at all is 401
vectors.description: This route accepts cookie OR bearer, but it does require one of them.

preconditions.session: no cookie and no Authorization header

vectors.notes: Contrast the discovery family in amm_registry_vectors.json, where hub-config, currencies, pairs, pool status and circuit-breaker status all answer 200 with no credential at all.

vectors.title: Committing liquidity without amount is 400
vectors.description: pool_pair and amount are both required despite the contract listing three further deprecated fields.
vectors.notes: This operation declares only 200, 400, 401 and 403 — no 404 and no 422. An unknown pool_pair therefore does not have a distinct documented status; that gap is recorded in the file README.

vectors.title: Reconciliation on an unconfigured gateway is 503
vectors.description: Deployment-shape signal, not a fault. The endpoint needs HUB_BESU_RPC_URL, W_TOKEN_ADDRESS and this Central Bank's hub address.

preconditions.gateway: hub RPC or W-token address unset

vectors.notes: A conformance runner should SKIP on 503 here rather than fail. Distinguish it from the 500 on the same route, which means the reconciliation itself failed — and whose cause is logged, not returned.

vectors.title: Deprecated identity fields in the body are accepted and ignored
vectors.description: Sending owner_bank_id, spoke_network, native_asset and mirrored_asset still succeeds, but none of the values is honoured. Caller identity is never taken from a request body anywhere on this platform.
vectors.notes: Assert the outcome, not the status: owner_bank_id in the RESPONSE must be the caller's own bank, never central_bank_z. spoke_network is the one field with a conditional path — gateway configuration wins, and the body value is consulted only when that configuration is unset, which is a deployment a client cannot detect.
